summary.name: Ardour
summary.one_liner: Ardour is a free, open-source digital audio workstation for recording, editing, mixing and mastering audio and MIDI on Linux, macOS and Windows.
use_cases: Editing and mixing multitrack audio sessions
Composing with MIDI and software instruments
Podcast and radio production with clip editing
Syncing audio to video for film soundtracks
Mixing and exporting music for streaming
summary.what_it_does: Ardour records audio and MIDI from interfaces, microphones and keyboards, and imports audio or MIDI from disk or the Freesound database. Its editing tools include cut, move, stretch, crossfade, transpose, quantize and swing, with unlimited undo/redo in one window. The mixer offers EQ, dynamics, sends, inserts, automation and floating point processing, and supports AudioUnit, LV2, VST2/VST3 and LADSPA plugins. It also provides transport sync via MIDI timecode, LTC, MIDI clock and JACK, Mackie Control and OSC control, plus video import with a frame-accurate thumbnail timeline.
notable: Open source and developed transparently by a worldwide team
Flexible any-to-any signal routing with sends, inserts and returns
Sample-accurate automation and sync to MIDI timecode, LTC and JACK
Video timeline with frame-by-frame thumbnails and audio locked to video frames
caveats: The page does not state a price for the software itself; the 'open source' label is taken from the page's description of the project.
